event.name: AutoCon 6
event.venue: The Westin La Paloma Resort & Spa
notes: Workshop wifi: use the Autocon6 SSID, which is set aside for workshops.
Many workshops offer a recording or remote option because of flight cancellations. Check the workshop's Slack channel.

workshops.title: Agentic NetOps in Tines: Moving from Brittle Scripts to Autonomous Workflows with Human-in-the-Loop Control
workshops.levels: Net Intermediate · Linux Beginner · Prog Intermediate
workshops.tldr: Build an agentic NetOps workflow in Tines that hooks LLMs and MCP up to telemetry for AI-driven triage, with guardrails and human approval gates.
prep: Log in to the Tines training tenant with the email you used for AutoCon. Use the link below if the invite email never arrived or went to spam.
Before the session, power on an always-on Cisco DevNet sandbox device that doesn't need VPN, and note its address and credentials.
notes: Session is being recorded. Remote Zoom link is in the Slack channel.

workshops.title: From Intent to Execution: Nautobot and Ansible, Better Together
workshops.levels: Net Intermediate · Linux Intermediate · Prog Intermediate
workshops.tldr: Use Nautobot as the source of truth driving Ansible/AWX: dynamic inventory, Config Contexts, Dynamic Groups, GraphQL-rendered configs, Job Buttons, writing state back, and event-triggered workflows with approval.
prep: Bring a laptop with a browser and a charger. Nothing to install.
Your cloud lab link and password arrive by email (Nautobot, AWX, two Arista switches).
You should have run an Ansible playbook before. No Nautobot, AWX or Python experience needed.
notes: AWX stands in for Ansible Automation Platform, so the concepts carry over directly.

workshops.title: Into the Unknown: Deep Dive into the Linux Network Stack
workshops.levels: Net Intermediate · Linux Beginner · Prog Beginner
workshops.tldr: Linux networking from bridges to OVS/OVN, plus eBPF, DPDK, switchdev offload, BGP/IS-IS/MPLS, EVPN/VXLAN and performance testing.
prep: The FAQ is a canvas in the Slack channel (also sent by email).
notes: Recorded. Slides and Containerlab files to run the labs locally are promised after the workshop.

workshops.title: Know Before You Deploy: Hands-On Network CI/CD with Forward Predict
workshops.levels: Net Intermediate · Linux Beginner · Prog Beginner
workshops.tldr: Build a CI/CD pipeline with GitHub Actions and Forward Predict that catches behaviour regressions before deployment.
prep: You need a browser and a GitHub account. The lab runs in a GitHub Codespace.
Get a seat at the link below (opened 08:30 Monday): press Get a seat, accept the GitHub invite, then open it in Codespaces.
Stuck? Post "@wsa4 help seat-NN" in Slack.
notes: Recorded. Zoom is for remote attendees only ("In room? No Zoom!").

workshops.title: Old Protocol, New Brain: Hands-On Troubleshooting with an AI-Native SSH Terminal
workshops.levels: Net Intermediate · Linux Beginner · Prog Beginner
workshops.tldr: Troubleshoot a Containerlab network with st-cli using natural language or plain commands, through guided failure scenarios with a human in the loop.

workshops.title: Design Driven Automation: Architect, Validate and Deploy an EVPN VXLAN Fabric with Arista AVD
workshops.levels: Net Intermediate · Linux Beginner · Prog Beginner
workshops.tldr: Architect, validate and deploy a leaf-spine EVPN/VXLAN fabric as code with arista.avd, pyavd and ANTA, covering Day 0 and Day 2 plus multi-vendor extension.

workshops.title: Who Gets the Truck Roll? Joining Telemetry, Topology, and a Graph through Discovery
workshops.levels: Net Intermediate · Linux Intermediate · Prog Beginner
workshops.tldr: Discover a multi-vendor network and join telemetry, inventory and topology in a graph database, on a hosted lab simulating an MPLS/PON backbone.
prep: A FAQ was promised by email.
notes: Jeff Cook is presenting remotely because of travel problems. Pieter van Os is in the room.
The whole workshop is hosted online, so you can also follow it remotely.

workshops.title: Building Network Automations with BackBox
workshops.levels: Net Intermediate · Linux Beginner · Prog Beginner
workshops.tldr: Build, test and deploy automations in BackBox (Kilter) in a live lab: backup, compliance, drift remediation, scheduling, and change verification with rollback.
notes: Remote Zoom details are in the Slack channel.

workshops.title: Loop Engineering, Spec Driven Development, and the Future of VibeOps
workshops.levels: Net Beginner · Linux Beginner · Prog Intermediate
workshops.tldr: Lectures on LLMs, Ralph loops and spec-driven development with GitHub Spec Kit, then build a networking game in teams of six and show it off.
prep: Set up your build environment from the repo before Tuesday so the session isn't spent on setup.
The FAQ PDF and the final slide deck (updated Mon 16 Nov) are in the Slack channel.
When you arrive, get a group-number sticker from John (10 teams of 6). Don't leave valuables where you first sit, because groups move.
agenda: Lecture: LLMs, Ralph loops, SDD and Spec Kit

workshops.title: Open Source Design-Driven Automation: From Fabric Intent to Running Config with Infrahub and AVD
workshops.levels: Net Intermediate · Linux Beginner · Prog Beginner
workshops.tldr: An open-source pipeline on the NAF framework: Infrahub as the intent source, AVD generating per-device config, and Ansible pushing to a Containerlab fabric.

workshops.title: Operationalizing SONiC in Modern Data Centers: Deployment, Telemetry, and Automation
workshops.levels: Net Beginner · Linux Beginner · Prog Beginner
workshops.tldr: Deploy a SONiC fabric from scratch in Containerlab, configure interfaces, BGP and EVPN, pull gNMI/OpenConfig telemetry, and get started automating it.
prep: Bring a laptop with an SSH client.
Make sure your work VPN doesn't block SSH to Google Cloud.
You get an instruction card and your own lab instance on the day.
notes: Lab instructions stay available afterwards in a repo shared during the workshop.

workshops.title: From Network Change to Code: A Hands-on Network as Code Workshop
workshops.levels: Net Beginner · Linux Beginner · Prog Beginner
workshops.tldr: Network as Code with Meraki APIs, Terraform and GitHub Actions, plus pre-change validation and Robot Framework testing.

workshops.title: AI for the Network Forward Engineer: Agents & Application Evaluation
workshops.levels: Net Intermediate · Linux Intermediate · Prog Intermediate
workshops.tldr: Build a network co-pilot on local and cloud LLMs in a browser lab: prompt engineering, Pydantic, a LangChain agent, a Streamlit UI, and evaluation and hallucination testing.
prep: Before Tuesday, launch the GitHub Codespace from the repo.
Get an Arize API key and space (see WORKSHOP_FAQ.md in the repo).
Watch the setup video ("AutoCon 6 Workshop - 0 Setting Up" on the Network Automation Nerds YouTube channel).
notes: Remote option will follow the official NAF Zoom setup.

workshops.title: Building a Network Source of Intent — From Architecture to Practice
workshops.levels: Net Beginner · Linux Intermediate · Prog Intermediate
workshops.tldr: Design and run a network source of truth with Infrahub and NAF: schema modelling, GraphQL, validation, branching, Generators and Jinja2 Transforms.

workshops.title: Digital Twinning at Scale
workshops.levels: Net Advanced · Linux Intermediate · Prog Intermediate
workshops.tldr: Emulate a 200+ router data centre fabric with Containerlab and FRRouting, covering numbering schemes, scripts versus templates, and scaling on limited compute.
prep: A FAQ went out by email.
notes: Expect it to be interactive and a bit messy: scripts are built live with Claude instead of showing finished work.

workshops.title: The Self Driving Network: From Drift Detection to Autonomous Remediation with Streaming Telemetry
workshops.levels: Net Intermediate · Linux Intermediate · Prog Intermediate
workshops.tldr: A closed loop that detects and automatically fixes config and state drift on a Containerlab network (Juniper cRPD, cSRX, Alpine), built from NAF framework pieces: NetBox/YAML/Excel intent, Telegraf/gNMI, InfluxDB/Kapacitor, a FastAPI orchestrator, PyEZ/Ansible, and Grafana/ntfy with approve/reject.
prep: Look for the email with your VM's SSH Host entry and private key.
Install VS Code and the Remote - SSH extension.
Test from your laptop: ssh naf-ac6-ws-vm
notes: Use cases: BGP peer-as drift, logging drift, a prefix-limit leak, and swap-a-block.
